a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every input type X, every output type Y, and every N of type S1 X Y, there exists an N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has exactly one index; this counts indices, not possible states. (2) For every ordered pair of distinct indices m and n of N′, it is not the case that there is both a nonempty directed chain of dependency steps from m to n and one from n to m. A step from i to j means that there exist two state assignments agreeing at every index other than i, and a common input, for which the updates at j differ. The assignments need not be reachable. Condition (2) is vacuous with one index and does not forbid self-dependence. (3) For every finite list of inputs in X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs after each starts from its own initial assignment and processes the list from left to right. The same N′ must work for all lists; equality of internal states or update functions is not required."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every input type X, every output type Y, and every N of type S1 X Y, there exists an N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has exactly one index; this counts indices, not possible states. (2) For every ordered pair of distinct indices m and n of N′, it is not the case that there is both a nonempty directed chain of dependency steps from m to n and one from n to m. A step from i to j means that there exist two state assignments agreeing at every index other than i, and a common input, for which the updates at j differ. The assignments need not be reachable. Condition (2) is vacuous with one index and does not forbid self-dependence. (3) For every finite list of inputs in X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs after each starts from its own initial assignment and processes the list from left to right. The same N′ must work for all lists; equality of internal states or update functions is not required.

judgement.summary: For every modeled system, the TARGET specifies a single one-unit twin that matches its output on every finite input list; the distinct-unit feedback condition is vacuous and permits self-dependence. Storing the whole state in that unit gives a possible witness, though the snippet defines the proposition rather than proving it, and the description correctly distinguishes this observation from Hanson and Walker’s flip-flop hierarchy and its Φ = 0 conclusion.
